title: Group by Property
prompt: A dashboard wants to group records by one field. Write a function that receives an array of objects and a property name, then returns an object whose keys are property values and whose values are arrays of matching records.

explanation.beginner:
Example: groupByProperty([{"id":1,"status":"open"},{"id":2,"status":"done"},{"id":3,"status":"open"}], "status") produces {"open":[{"id":1,"status":"open"},{"id":3,"status":"open"}],"done":[{"id":2,"status":"done"}]}. Read the grouping key from each record. Create that key’s bucket once and append matching records in their original order.

Compare “handles empty arrays”: input [[],"status"] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Read the grouping key from each record. Create that key’s bucket once and append matching records in their original order.

Tempting mistake: Assigning bucket = [row] on every visit discards previous members of the same group.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. A one-pass grouping uses expected O(n) time and O(n) output references.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
